subject: SLA framework and loss-allocation / latency guardrails for HelioPay cutover
messages:
From: Aaron Schultz <aaron.schultz@heliopay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioPay Procurement <procurement@heliopay.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA clarifications for planned production cutover

Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is ready to proceed with the September cutover but procurement has a few outstanding questions about the SLA language in your template. Before legal drafts the PO we'd like to confirm:

1) How do monthly credits scale for multi-day partial outages (e.g., sustained increased error rates vs total downtime)?
2) Do you have a latency SLO that triggers credits or is crediting strictly availability-based? Our payments flow is latency-sensitive.
3) Is there a hard cap on credits we should expect per month (we need to plan for risk allocation)?

If you can send a proposed mapping (uptime bands, latency tiers, cap) we can circulate internally and give fast feedback.

Appreciate it — aim to finalize this before Sept 15.

— Aaron
Aaron Schultz
Head of Platform Ops, HelioPay
aaron.schultz@heliopay.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Schultz <aaron.schultz@heliopay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for planned production cutover
Attachments: redwood-sla-proposal-2026.pdf (application/pdf, 124KB)

Aaron — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise proposal that maps uptime bands, a simple latency-sensitivity overlay, and a monthly credit cap. Summary below (high level):

- Availability bands (monthly uptime % based on a 30-day window):
  * >= 99.95%: no credits
  * 99.50%–99.95%: 5% monthly service credit
  * 99.00%–99.49%: 15% monthly service credit
  * < 99.00%: 30% monthly service credit
- Latency sensitivity (applies to API p99 for request paths you identify):
  * p99 < 350ms: treated as within SLO (no credit)
  * p99 350–700ms: isolated latency credit (5%) if sustained > 12 hours in the month
  * p99 > 700ms: treated as severe latency; can trigger up to 15% credit if coupled with availability issues
- Monthly credit cap: 50% of the month’s recurring invoice for hosted inference (we can set different caps for Dedicated/Private)
- Carveouts: planned maintenance with >= 48h notice, regulatory takedowns, force majeure, and customer misconfigurations excluded

Notes and asks:
- We recommend you flag 2–3 high-sensitivity endpoints (payment auth, settlement) so we can attach p99 measurement and alerting to those routes — that is required for latency-based credits.
- Credit windows are based on our metrics pipeline (ingestion + aggregation). We include root-cause notes and a remediation plan with any credit issuance.

If this looks broadly acceptable I can loop legal and propose contract language and a cap table we can sign off.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for planned production cutover

Couple of internal implementation points (for your awareness, Monica):

- 50% monthly cap is OK for Hosted but conservative for Dedicated — for Dedicated customers we usually accept a 100% invoice cap if they've reserved capacity (different product line). If HelioPay is going Dedicated, we should flag product terms.
- Latency credit windows as written are operationally messy: "sustained > 12 hours" needs clearer definition — is that contiguous 12 hours, rolling 12-hour window, or 12 non-contiguous hours aggregated? My recommendation: contiguous 6-hour window or aggregated 12 hours but only if above severity threshold in at least one contiguous 6-hour block.
- Measurement source: we should explicitly call out primary metrics (our internal telemetry) and a secondary audit (customer logs) with reconciliation steps.

I'll join legal call if they want implementation detail.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Schultz <aaron.schultz@heliopay.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for planned production cutover

Aaron — following Monica's draft and internal notes from Ben, suggested edits for contract language:

1) Monthly credit table (revised):
   - >= 99.95%: 0% credit
   - 99.75%–99.94%: 5%
   - 99.00%–99.74%: 15%
   - < 99.00%: 30%
   *Rationale: narrows mid-tier to reduce churn from short blips while preserving stronger recourse for larger outages.*

2) Latency: define p99 window and trigger:
   - Trigger if p99 for nominated route exceeds threshold for a contiguous 6-hour period OR aggregated 12 hours across the month with at least one contiguous 3-hour block above threshold.
   - Latency-only credits cannot exceed 15% unless there is an availability breach.

3) Credit caps:
   - Hosted: 50% cap (as proposed)
   - Dedicated: cap equal to 100% of monthly committed spend (if customer has Dedicated reserved capacity)

4) Dispute window: customer has 30 days to raise metric disputes with audit log links; after 30 days metrics are final for that month.

If you confirm HelioPay's deployment type and nominate sensitive routes, we can bake final language and run DocuSign.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Schultz <aaron.schultz@heliopay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for planned production cutover
Attachments: heliopay-procurement-form.pdf (application/pdf, 98KB)

Thanks — these are helpful, and the revised bands look reasonable. A few items from our side before we sign:

- Deployment: HelioPay will be Hosted for the first 12 months with a view to move to Dedicated in Q4 2027.
- Sensitive routes: we will nominate three routes (payment-auth, settlement-commit, risk-eval) by EOD Sept 9; those will be the p99-tracked endpoints for latency credits.
- Cap ask: would you consider a 75% hosted cap instead of 50% as a fair compromise? We are asking our finance team for lower risk exposure but prefer a middle ground.

Assuming we can agree on the cap tweak, we'll sign — request to run the final doc through DocuSign next.

On the measurement/dispute flow: can you confirm the metric audit link will include raw p99 time series for nominated routes (we will cross-check with our side)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Aaron
Aaron Schultz
Head of Platform Ops, HelioPay
